package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.rememberScrollState
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.foundation.verticalScroll
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose.viewModel
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.ProductRepository
import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.data.priceLabel

@Composable
fun CheckoutScreen(
    productId: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val product = ProductRepository.cached(productId)

    Column(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
            .padding(16.dp)
            .testTag("checkout_screen"),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
    ) {
        if (product != null) {
            Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
                Row(Modifier.padding(16.dp), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
                    Text("${product.emoji} ${product.name}", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
                    Text(product.priceLabel(), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, modifier = Modifier.testTag("checkout_total"))
                }
            }
        }

        Text("Delivery details", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        CheckoutField("Full name", vm.name, { vm.name = it }, "field_name")
        CheckoutField("Email", vm.email, { vm.email = it }, "field_email", KeyboardType.Email)
        CheckoutField("Phone", vm.phone, { vm.phone = it }, "field_phone", KeyboardType.Phone)
        CheckoutField("Address", vm.address, { vm.address = it }, "field_address")
        CheckoutField("City", vm.city, { vm.city = it }, "field_city")
        CheckoutField("Pincode", vm.pincode, { vm.pincode = it }, "field_pincode", KeyboardType.Number)
    }
}

@Composable
private fun CheckoutField(
    label: String,
    value: String,
    onChange: (String) -> Unit,
    tag: String,
    keyboard: KeyboardType = KeyboardType.Text,
) {
    OutlinedTextField(
        value = value,
        onValueChange = onChange,
        label = { Text(label) },
        singleLine = true,
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = keyboard),
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag(tag),
    )
}

input.content:
# MonkeyMart

A small Android shopping app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) with three screens: shop list → item detail → checkout.

It is the demo target for [droid-monkey](https://github.com/shubhasai/droid-monkey), an agent that attacks Android apps with real-world faults, fixes what breaks, and proves each fix by replaying the attack. MonkeyMart contains **four deliberately planted lifecycle bugs**, so every droid-monkey run has a known right answer. droid-monkey itself is not specific to this app.

## Planted bugs

The `planted-bugs` tag marks the baseline with all four bugs present. Each bug arrived with the feature commit that introduced it.

| Fault | Where | What happens | Correct fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rotation | `ui/DetailScreen.kt`, `DealLoader` | The deal popup is shown from a `GlobalScope` job holding the Activity that started it. Rotating during the 5 s load crashes: `IllegalStateException: FragmentManager has been destroyed` | Lifecycle-aware scope (e.g. `viewModelScope`/`LaunchedEffect`), state in a ViewModel, no captured Activity |
| Process death | `ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt` | The six checkout fields are plain `mutableStateOf` with no `SavedStateHandle`. After the OS kills the app in the background, the user returns to an empty form (lost state, no crash) | `SavedStateHandle` (or `rememberSaveable`) |
| Network loss | `data/OrderRepository.kt`, `CheckoutViewModel.placeOrder` | `submit()` throws `IOException` when offline and nothing catches it: `java.io.IOException` crash | Catch the error, show a retry state, keep the form |
| Permission revoke | `ui/CouponScanner.kt` | A cached `camera_granted` flag in SharedPreferences is trusted after the user revokes the camera permission: `SecurityException` from `openCamera` | Check the permission at use time, request it again |

## Reproducing by hand

Needs a running emulator and `adb` on PATH.

```bash
./gradlew :app:installDebug
repro/run_all.sh          # one line per bug, about 2 minutes
repro/rotation.sh         # or any single bug
```

Verified on the `Pixel_10` AVD (Android 16, API 36):

```
rotation           crashed: java.lang.IllegalStateException
process_death      lost state: checkout form empty after relaunch
network_loss       crashed: java.io.IOException
permission_revoke  crashed: java.lang.SecurityException
```

Notes from building the repros, which droid-monkey's attacks also follow:

- Launch like a launcher tap (`MAIN`/`LAUNCHER`, `NEW_TASK|RESET_TASK_IF_NEEDED`). Otherwise a relaunch starts a new task and saved state is never restored.
- `am kill` only works once the app is in the background. Confirm the PID is gone before you judge the result.
- Android 16 can restore an app's last orientation on launch even with rotation locked, so set the rotation and wait until the display reports it.
- `pm revoke` kills the app process.

neatlogs is an **observability tool for AI agents**. It records everything the agent does as a tree of timed steps so you can open a run later and see exactly what happened: what the model was given, what it decided, which tools it called, how long each step took, and what it cost. For droid-monkey it does two jobs: debugging while we build, and producing the evidence judges score (partner tools are 25% of the score).

## The core ideas

| Term | Meaning | In droid-monkey |
|---|---|---|
| **Trace** | One complete run, shown as a tree | One `droid-monkey run`, or one attack |
| **Span** | One timed step inside a trace, with inputs, outputs, duration and metadata. Spans nest | A LangGraph node, an adb command, a Claude call, a `claude -p` fix |
| **Span kind** | The type of step: `WORKFLOW` (a top-level job), `TOOL` (a tool call), plus LLM spans created automatically | `WORKFLOW` for the run, `TOOL` for adb, Gradle and `claude -p` |
| **workflow_name** | Groups traces by which agent produced them | `droid-monkey` (the spike used `droid-monkey-spike`) |
| **tags** | Labels for filtering | `attack:rotation`, `app:com.shubhasai.monkeymart`, `prompt:v2` |
| **session_id** | Links several traces into one session | The run ID, so all attacks of one run group together |

## How it plugs into the code

The setup we tested in Block 0:

```python
import neatlogs
neatlogs.init(                       # must run BEFORE importing langgraph/langchain/anthropic
    workflow_name="droid-monkey",
    instrumentations=["langgraph", "langchain", "anthropic"],
    tags=["run:abc123"],
)                                    # API key comes from NEATLOGS_API_KEY in .env

from neatlogs import span

@span(kind="TOOL", name="adb_inject", tool_name="adb")
def kill_app(): ...                  # our own steps get wrapped by hand

neatlogs.flush(); neatlogs.shutdown()   # at exit, so nothing is lost
```

There are two ways spans get recorded:
- **Automatically:** once `init` has run, every LangGraph node and every Claude call (prompt, reply, tokens) is recorded with no extra code.
- **By hand with `@span`:** for the things neatlogs can't see, like adb, Gradle, and the `claude -p` subprocess. For `claude -p`, we copy the session ID, token counts and cost from its JSON output onto the span.

## What we confirmed in Block 0

- It installs with `neatlogs[langchain,langgraph,anthropic]` (version 1.4.26).
- Graph nodes, Haiku calls and a hand-made `TOOL` span ran in one process. The SDK reported **0 export failures**, so the data reached neatlogs.
- **Still unchecked:** whether the dashboard shows these as one nested tree or as separate flat traces. That's the dashboard check I asked you for earlier. It decides whether I need to add manual parent spans in Block 3.

## The trace for one droid-monkey run

```
WORKFLOW  droid-monkey run  (session = run id, tags: app, avd)
├── node scout          → TOOL adb uiautomator dump ×N
├── node plan           → LLM Haiku 5.5: "process_death first because…"
├── WORKFLOW attack: process_death          (tag attack:process_death)
│   ├── node inject     → TOOL adb am kill, TOOL relaunch
│   ├── node observe    → TOOL logcat, TOOL ui dump · verdict=lost_state
│   ├── node decide     → LLM Haiku: "diagnose" (reasoning stored)
│   ├── node diagnose   → LLM Haiku + TOOL entire graph search
│   ├── node fix        → TOOL claude -p  (session id, tokens, cost, checkpoint id)
│   └── node verify     → TOOL gradle build, TOOL replay attack, TOOL test · fixed ✓
├── WORKFLOW attack: rotation …
│   └── fix failed → retry: node diagnose (new hypothesis) → fix → verify ✓
└── node report
```

Each attack also gets **its own trace link**, which goes into the PR's evidence table.

## Why it matters for the score

The PRD's judging checklist asks for three things from neatlogs. Here's how we produce each:

| Required evidence | How we get it |
|---|---|
| **A trace link for each attack** in the PR | `report.py` writes the link into the PR table. *Open question:* how to get a trace URL from the SDK. I'll check the docs and the dashboard in Block 3 |
| **A before/after pair with numbers** | Run the same attacks twice: once with a naive brief (whole repo), once with the graph-plugin brief. Compare fix success and tokens per attack. Tags like `prompt:v1` / `prompt:v2` keep the two runs apart |
| **One trace showing a failure and recovery** | `--fail-first-fix` forces a failed fix, and the trace shows the failed verify, the new hypothesis, the resumed coder session, and the passing verify |

It also feeds the **cfo.ai plan**: cost per attack (Haiku tokens plus the `claude -p` cost) comes straight from these spans.

## Other SDK features worth using

These are from the SDK's API. I haven't tested them yet.

- **Prompt management** (`create_prompt`, `get_prompt`, `save_as_version`): store the planner and diagnoser prompts as versions in neatlogs. That's a clean way to show "prompt v1 vs v2" in the before/after comparison.
- **Masking and PII** (`mask=`, `pii_enabled`): stack traces and screen dumps can contain user data, so we can strip emails, phone numbers and tokens before upload. MonkeyMart's form holds a name, phone and address, so it's relevant even in the demo.
- **`capture_logs`, `sample_rate`, delivery diagnostics:** useful for debugging the tracing itself.

The one thing I need from you: open the **`droid-monkey-spike`** workflow in neatlogs and tell me whether a run shows up as **one nested tree** (plan → inject → decide, with the Haiku calls inside) or as **separate flat entries**. That decides how much manual span work Block 3 needs.

## What gets built

```
droid-monkey/src/droid_monkey/
├── tools/
│   ├── adb.py        every adb call, with a timeout and one retry; raises AdbHang for the Watchdog
│   ├── emulator.py   find/boot the AVD, wait for boot_completed, health check, restart
│   ├── device.py     the verified actions learned in Block 1 (below)
│   ├── ui.py         screen dump → parsed nodes, find/tap elements, read editable fields
│   ├── logcat.py     clear all buffers, read the crash buffer, parse the exception and app stack frames
│   └── gradle.py     build, install, find the APK and package, run one test class
├── attacks/
│   ├── base.py       the attack lifecycle: prepare → snapshot → inject → observe → restore
│   ├── process_death.py
│   ├── rotation.py
│   ├── network_loss.py
│   └── permission_revoke.py
├── observe.py        the verdict: crashed / lost_state / survived, plus evidence
├── config.py         loads monkey.yaml
└── cli.py            `droid-monkey attack <name>`
```

Plus `monkey.yaml` in the **MonkeyMart** repo. That's the only place MonkeyMart's details live.

## `device.py`: the Block 1 lessons as code

Each of these was a silent failure in Block 1, where the test reported "no bug" when there was one:

| Function | What it does | The trap it avoids |
|---|---|---|
| `launch()` | Finds the app's launcher activity itself (`cmd package resolve-activity`) and starts it like a launcher tap | A plain `am start` opens a new task, so saved state is never restored |
| `kill_in_background()` | Sends the app home, then repeats `am kill` until the process is confirmed gone | `am kill` does nothing while the app is in the foreground |
| `set_rotation(target)` | Sets the rotation and waits until the display reports it. Always flips relative to the current orientation | Android 16 restores the app's last orientation on launch |
| `network(off/on)` | Turns wifi and mobile data off, waits until the device is really offline | Firing the action before the network has actually dropped |
| `runtime_permissions()` | Reads the app's granted runtime permissions from `dumpsys package` | Hard-coding CAMERA for MonkeyMart |
| `restore()` | Network on, rotation back, permissions re-granted, **always run in a `finally`** | One failed attack breaking every attack after it |

## `ui.py`: reading the screen for any app

- Parses the screen dump into nodes: id, class, text, description, bounds, editable, scrollable.
- **Finds elements** by resource ID, then text, then content description, so apps without test tags still work.
- **Collects every editable field's value by scrolling** the scrollable container top to bottom. Block 1 showed that off-screen fields disappear from the dump, and that looks exactly like lost state.
- Takes a screen fingerprint (which screen this is) and a screenshot.
- Each screen dump takes 1–2 seconds, so attacks never poll the screen inside a timing window.

## The four attacks

Each one first gets to a target screen. In Block 2 that uses the step list in `monkey.yaml`; in Block 3 Scout and the model handle navigation. Then it runs one of these:

| Attack | Inject | Then | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **process_death** | Snapshot the fields → Home → confirmed kill → launch like a launcher tap | Collect the fields again | Fields emptied → `lost_state`. Crash → `crashed` |
| **rotation** | Fire the trigger action (e.g. open the detail screen), wait briefly, flip the rotation, confirm the relaunch | Wait out the trigger's delay | Crash → `crashed`. Changed fields → `lost_state` |
| **network_loss** | Network off and confirmed | Fire the trigger action (e.g. "Place order") | Crash → `crashed` |
| **permission_revoke** | For each granted runtime permission: revoke it (the app gets killed), relaunch, return to the screen | Fire the action that uses it | Crash → `crashed` |

The **verdict is decided only by code**: a crash or ANR for this app in the crash buffer, or a field diff. AI only *explains* results, from Block 3 on.

## MonkeyMart's `monkey.yaml` (app-specific, lives in MonkeyMart)

```yaml
package: com.shubhasai.monkeymart
module: app
avd: Pixel_10
targets:                       # Block 2: hand-written. Block 3: Scout + model find these
  checkout:
    steps: [tap product_3, tap android:id/button1, tap buy_now]
    fill: true                 # type sample values into every editable field
  detail_loading:
    steps: [tap product_3]
actions:                       # which tap fires the risky operation on each screen
  checkout: tap place_order
  coupon: tap scan_coupon
```

droid-monkey only reads this file. Pointing it at another app means writing a different `monkey.yaml`, not changing code.

## Tests and evidence

- **Unit tests** (pytest) on saved real outputs: a screen dump from MonkeyMart, a crash log, a `dumpsys package` output. They run in seconds without the emulator.
- **Evidence for each attack** goes in `monkey-report/<run>/<attack>/`: `before.png`, `after.png`, `before.xml`, `after.xml`, `logcat.txt`, `verdict.json`. The PR table and the dashboard later read from these.

## Time and risks

- **Estimate: about 2.5–3 hours.** It's about 16:45 now and the plan had Block 2 at 19:30, so we're roughly 3 hours ahead.
- **Risks:**

  - The rotation attack needs the trigger to start a slow operation. That's generic ("fire an action, then rotate mid-flight"), but on other apps it depends on the planner picking a good action. That's Block 3's job.

import subprocess

from .adb import Adb, AdbError


@dataclass
class BuildResult:
    ok: bool
    seconds: float
    apk: Path | None
    log_tail: str


def _variant_task(module: str, variant: str, verb: str) -> str:
    return f":{module}:{verb}{variant[:1].upper()}{variant[1:]}"


def build(app_dir: Path, module: str = "app", variant: str = "debug", timeout: float = 900) -> BuildResult:
    start = time.time()
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["./gradlew", _variant_task(module, variant, "assemble"), "--console=plain", "-q"],
        cwd=app_dir, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
    )
    apks = sorted((app_dir / module / "build" / "outputs" / "apk" / variant).glob("*.apk"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    tail = "\n".join((proc.stdout + proc.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-40:])
    return BuildResult(proc.returncode == 0, time.time() - start, apks[-1] if apks else None, tail)


def install(adb: Adb, apk: Path) -> None:
    out = adb.run("install", "-r", "-t", str(apk), timeout=180)
    if "Success" not in out:

"""monkey.yaml: everything app-specific lives here, never in droid-monkey's code."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

CONFIG_NAME = "monkey.yaml"


@dataclass
class Target:
    """A screen state to attack, reached by replaying steps from launch."""
    name: str
    steps: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    fill: bool = False  # type sample values into every editable field once there


@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """Default target and trigger action for one attack. The planner chooses these from Block 3 on."""
    target: str
    action: str | None = None
    settle_seconds: float = 4.0


@dataclass
class AppConfig:
    app_dir: Path
    package: str
    module: str = "app"
    variant: str = "debug"
    avd: str | None = None
    targets: dict[str, Target] = field(default_factory=dict)
    scenarios: dict[str, Scenario] = field(default_factory=dict)
    fill_values: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


def load(app_dir: Path) -> AppConfig:
    path = app_dir / CONFIG_NAME
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{path} not found. Run `droid-monkey init` in the app's repo first.")
    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}
    targets = {name: Target(name=name, steps=list(t.get("steps", [])), fill=bool(t.get("fill", False)))
               for name, t in (raw.get("targets") or {}).items()}
    scenarios = {name: Scenario(target=s["target"], action=s.get("action"),
                                settle_seconds=float(s.get("settle_seconds", 4.0)))
                 for name, s in (raw.get("scenarios") or {}).items()}
    return AppConfig(
        app_dir=app_dir.resolve(),
        package=raw["package"],
        module=raw.get("module", "app"),
        variant=raw.get("variant", "debug"),
        avd=raw.get("avd"),
        targets=targets,
        scenarios=scenarios,
        fill_values=dict(raw.get("fill_values") or {}),
    )

"""Process death: the OS kills the app in the background, the user comes back."""

import time

from ..observe import classify
from .base import Attack


class ProcessDeath(Attack):
    name = "process_death"

    def execute(self, scenario):
        self.prepare(scenario)
        before = self.fields()
        before_screen = self.snapshot("before")
        self.fire(scenario.action)

        self.device.kill_in_background()  # verified: the process is really gone
        self.device.launch()               # like returning from recents
        self.device.set_rotation(0)
        time.sleep(2)

        crashes = self.crashes()
        after_screen = self.snapshot("after")
        after = {} if crashes else self.fields()
        restored = self._same_screen(before_screen, after_screen)
        return classify(crashes, before, after, screen_restored=restored), before, after

    def _same_screen(self, a, b) -> bool:
        fa, fb = a.fingerprint(self.cfg.package), b.fingerprint(self.cfg.package)
        if not fa:
            return True
        return len(fa & fb) / len(fa | fb) >= 0.5

"""Rotation: a configuration change recreates the Activity, possibly while work is in flight."""

import time

from ..observe import classify
from .base import Attack

IN_FLIGHT_DELAY = 1.0  # rotate this long after the trigger, while its work is still running


class Rotation(Attack):
    name = "rotation"

    def execute(self, scenario):
        target = self.prepare(scenario)
        before = self.fields() if target.fill else {}
        self.snapshot("before")

        self.fire(scenario.action)
        if scenario.action:
            time.sleep(IN_FLIGHT_DELAY)  # no screen dumps here: each one takes 1-2 s
        self.device.flip_rotation()      # verified: the display reports the new rotation
        time.sleep(scenario.settle_seconds)

        crashes = self.crashes()
        self.snapshot("after")
        after = self.fields() if (before and not crashes) else {}
        return classify(crashes, before, after), before, after

"""Network loss: connectivity drops right before the user triggers a network operation."""

import time

from ..observe import classify
from .base import Attack


class NetworkLoss(Attack):
    name = "network_loss"

    def execute(self, scenario):
        target = self.prepare(scenario)
        before = self.fields() if target.fill else {}
        self.snapshot("before")

        self.device.set_network(False)  # verified: no active default network
        self.fire(scenario.action)
        time.sleep(scenario.settle_seconds)

        crashes = self.crashes()
        self.snapshot("after")
        after = self.fields() if (before and not crashes) else {}
        return classify(crashes, before, after), before, after

"""Permission revoke: the user grants a permission, later revokes it in Settings, then uses the feature again."""

import time

from ..observe import SKIPPED, Verdict, classify
from .base import Attack


class PermissionRevoke(Attack):
    name = "permission_revoke"

    def execute(self, scenario):
        target = self.prepare(scenario, clear_data=True)  # first-time user: nothing granted, nothing cached
        granted_before = self.device.runtime_permissions()

        # 1. Use the feature once, granting whatever it asks for through the app's own flow.
        self.fire(scenario.action)
        if self.accept_permission_dialog():
            self.notes.append("granted the permission prompt on first use")
        time.sleep(2)
        if crashes := self.crashes():
            return classify(crashes, {}, {}), {}, {}

        granted_after = self.device.runtime_permissions()
        newly = [p for p, g in granted_after.items() if g and not granted_before.get(p)]
        to_revoke = newly or [p for p, g in granted_after.items() if g]
        if not to_revoke:
            return Verdict(SKIPPED, "the action did not use any runtime permission"), {}, {}
        self.notes.append(f"revoking: {', '.join(to_revoke)}")
        self.snapshot("before")

        # 2. The user revokes it in Settings; Android kills the app. Then they come back and try again.
        for perm in to_revoke:
            self.device.revoke(perm)
        time.sleep(1)
        from ..tools import logcat
        logcat.clear(self.adb)
        self.device.launch()
        self.device.set_rotation(0)
        if not self._action_on_screen(scenario.action):
            self.navigate(target)
        self.fire(scenario.action)
        time.sleep(scenario.settle_seconds)

        crashes = self.crashes()
        self.snapshot("after")
        return classify(crashes, {}, {}), {}, {}

    def _action_on_screen(self, action: str | None) -> bool:
        if not action or " " not in action:
            return False
        from ..tools import ui
        return ui.dump(self.adb).find(action.split(" ", 1)[1]) is not None

from .base import Attack, AttackResult, Context
from .network_loss import NetworkLoss
from .permission_revoke import PermissionRevoke
from .process_death import ProcessDeath
from .rotation import Rotation

CATALOGUE: dict[str, type[Attack]] = {
    a.name: a for a in (ProcessDeath, Rotation, NetworkLoss, PermissionRevoke)
}

__all__ = ["Attack", "AttackResult", "Context", "CATALOGUE"]

"""Scenario generation from a screen map: generic rules, no app knowledge."""

from droid_monkey.explorer import ActionInfo, ScreenInfo, ScreenMap
from droid_monkey.scenarios import best, generate


def sample_map() -> ScreenMap:
    home = ScreenInfo("s0", [], "Home", [], ["list"], [
        ActionInfo("row_#", "First row", "row_#", effect="new_screen", to_screen="s1", settle_seconds=5, showed_progress=True),
        ActionInfo("text:Help", "Help", "help", effect="same_screen", settle_seconds=0.1),
    ])
    detail = ScreenInfo("s1", ["tap row_1"], "Detail", [], ["title"], [
        ActionInfo("open_form", "Edit", "open_form", effect="new_screen", to_screen="s2", settle_seconds=0.2),
    ])
    form = ScreenInfo("s2", ["tap row_1", "tap open_form"], "Profile", ["name", "email", "phone"], ["name", "email"], [
        ActionInfo("save", "Save", "save", effect="new_screen", to_screen="s3", settle_seconds=2, showed_progress=True),
        ActionInfo("avatar", "Photo", "avatar", effect="permission", permissions=["android.permission.CAMERA"]),
    ])
    return ScreenMap("com.example", {s.id: s for s in (home, detail, form)})


def test_every_attack_gets_a_candidate_with_a_reason():
    cands = generate(sample_map())
    for attack in ("process_death", "rotation", "network_loss", "permission_revoke"):
        c = best(cands, attack)
        assert c is not None and c.reason, attack


def test_best_candidates_follow_the_generic_rules():
    cands = generate(sample_map())
    assert best(cands, "process_death").screen == "s2"           # the form has the most to lose
    assert best(cands, "network_loss").action == "tap save"      # submitting a form with a progress indicator
    assert best(cands, "permission_revoke").action == "tap avatar"
    assert best(cands, "rotation").action == "tap row_#"          # longest in-flight work


def test_fast_actions_are_not_rotation_or_network_targets():
    cands = generate(sample_map())
    assert not any(c.action == "tap text:Help" for c in cands)


def test_map_round_trips_through_json(tmp_path):
    smap = sample_map()
    smap.save(tmp_path / "map.json")
    again = ScreenMap.load(tmp_path / "map.json")
    assert again.screens["s2"].fields == ["name", "email", "phone"]
    assert again.screens["s2"].actions[1].permissions == ["android.permission.CAMERA"]

content.text:
Block 2 is done, and the attacks are no longer app-specific. On MonkeyMart, with a `monkey.yaml` that only holds the package name, the build settings and the emulator name, droid-monkey found all four planted bugs and gave the expected verdict for each.

**How it works now:**
1. **`droid-monkey explore`** clears the app's data, then taps every distinct clickable element on each screen it reaches. Repeated list items count once. For each tap it records the result: new screen, popup, permission prompt, slow work, leaving the app, or crash. It saves a screen map with a replayable path to each screen. On MonkeyMart it found 4 screens in about 4 minutes.
2. **`scenarios.py`** turns that map into ranked attack candidates, each with a plain reason (e.g. "'Scan coupon' asks for CAMERA; using it again after a revoke must not crash").
3. **`droid-monkey attack all`** runs the top candidate for each attack:

| Attack | Picked automatically | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| network_loss | "Place order" submits a form | crashed: `IOException` at `OrderRepository.kt:27` |
| permission_revoke | "Scan coupon" asks for CAMERA | crashed: `SecurityException` at `CouponScanner.kt:44` |
| process_death | checkout form with 6 fields | lost_state, 6/6 fields emptied |
| rotation | tapping a product starts 5s of work | crashed: `IllegalStateException` at `DetailScreen.kt:64` |

**Checks:**
- **No false alarms:** rotating the filled checkout form, and killing the app on the shop list, both came back "survived".
- **No app names in the code:** a search of droid-monkey's source for MonkeyMart's package and element names finds nothing.
- **Unit tests:** all 10 pass. One strips every resource ID from a real screen dump to simulate an app without test tags. Another builds candidates for a made-up app.
- **Commits:** both repos are pushed, with no Claude trailer.

**Limits to know about:**
- **Exploration clears the app's data** so first-use permission prompts show up. Apps behind a login need `entry_steps` (a test-account login) in `monkey.yaml`.
- **Speed:** each screen read takes 1–2 seconds, so a full exploration plus all attacks takes about 8 minutes on MonkeyMart. That's fine for one run, but Block 3 should reuse the saved map instead of exploring every time.
- **The `planted-bugs` tag is now one commit behind MonkeyMart's `main`,** because `monkey.yaml` was added after it. The app code is identical. Agent runs will branch from `main`; if you'd rather move the tag, that needs a force-push, which you'd run yourself.
- **Not yet proven on a second, unrelated app.** That stays in Block 5.

**Next is Block 3:** the AI loop on top of this. The model plans and orders the candidates, decides after each result, diagnoses using the crash location plus Entire's code graph, has `claude -p` fix the bug, and the code verifies the fix by replaying the same attack. All of it is traced in neatlogs.

Also still open: what the `droid-monkey-spike` traces look like in neatlogs, one nested tree or flat entries. That decides how Block 3 sets up tracing.
why attack folder is there ?

There are two folders it could be, so here's each.

## `droid-monkey/src/droid_monkey/attacks/`: the fault types

This folder holds **one file per kind of real-world fault**. These files describe *how to break any Android app*, not *where to break MonkeyMart*:

| File | What it knows (the same for every app) |
|---|---|
| `base.py` | The lifecycle every attack shares: get to the screen → snapshot → inject → observe → **always restore the device**. Also navigation, form filling and evidence saving |
| `process_death.py` | How to kill an app the way Android does (Home, then a confirmed `am kill`), bring it back, and compare the fields |
| `rotation.py` | How to rotate while work is running and confirm the rotation actually applied |
| `network_loss.py` | How to cut wifi and data, confirm the device is offline, then fire the action |
| `permission_revoke.py` | How to let the app ask for a permission, revoke it the way Settings does, and use the feature again |

The **where** (which screen, which button) comes from the explorer's screen map at runtime. None of these files mentions a MonkeyMart screen or button. The search I ran confirmed there are no app names anywhere in the source.

Keeping one file per fault is the PRD's design (`attacks/process_death.py`, `rotation.py`, …). Adding a new fault type means adding one file, with no changes to the orchestrator. The P1 attacks (low memory, cold start, ANR) would each be one more file here.

## `MonkeyMart/monkey-report/attack-.../`: run evidence

If you meant the folders appearing under `MonkeyMart/monkey-report/` (`attack-20261011-…`, `dev-pd`, `generic-all`, `explore-…`), those are **output**, not code. Each `droid-monkey` run saves its evidence there: before and after screenshots, screen dumps, the crash log, `verdict.json`, and the screen map.

- They're **git-ignored**, so they never get committed by accident.
- The `dev-*` ones are leftovers from my testing today. I can delete them.
- In Block 5, `report.py` will write one curated `monkey-report/<run-id>/` for the final run, which gets committed for the PR.

You're partly right. There are no MonkeyMart names in those files, but **a few values in them were tuned while I tested on MonkeyMart**. On another app they could miss a bug, which makes them less generic than I claimed.

**What's generic:** each file is a fault *mechanism* that works the same on any Android app: kill the process the way Android does, rotate the screen, cut the network, revoke a permission. Which screen and which button come from the explorer's map.

**Where they're not generic yet:**

| Where | Problem | What could go wrong on another app |
|---|---|---|
| `rotation.py`: `IN_FLIGHT_DELAY = 1.0` | Always rotates 1 s after the tap. That fits MonkeyMart's 5 s load | If the work takes 0.8 s, the rotation lands after it's finished: a false "survived" |
| `base.py`: `DEFAULT_FILL` | Sample values are guessed from field IDs (`email`, `phone`, `pin`…), with "Test 123" for anything else. That fits MonkeyMart's field names | A field with no ID gets "Test 123"; an email check rejects it and the submit button never enables, so the attack never fires |
| `process_death.py`, `permission_revoke.py` | Fixed waits (2 s after relaunch, 2 s after granting) | A slower app isn't ready yet, and the result is judged too early |
| `network_loss.py` | Only treats a **crash** as a failure | An app that quietly does nothing offline (no error, no retry) counts as "survived" |
| `permission_revoke.py` | Wipes the app's data first (`pm clear`), and only knows the standard Android permission dialog button IDs | A logged-in app loses its session; an OEM dialog may not be recognised |
| The 4 attack types | A fixed list, by PRD design | That's intentional. New faults are new files, so it's not a genericity problem |

**How I'd fix each:**
1. **Rotation timing from the map:** rotate at about 25% of the work time the explorer measured for that action, not a fixed 1 s.
2. **Form filling from the field's own hints:** read the input type and label the app gives each field (email, number, phone, password), and confirm the submit button actually enabled. If it didn't, report "couldn't fill this form" instead of a misleading result.
3. **Wait for the screen to settle,** using the explorer's settle logic, instead of fixed sleeps.
4. **Network loss also checks for silent failure:** after the action, check whether the app showed *something* (error text, retry button, snackbar) or did nothing. Doing nothing becomes a finding (`no_feedback`) rather than "survived".
5. **No data wipe when the app has `entry_steps` (a login),** and recognise permission dialogs by their package rather than exact button IDs.

That's about 45 minutes, and it's worth doing before Block 3, since the AI loop sits on top of these verdicts. Should I go ahead?
attack type should be dynamic and based on app right ?

Partly. **Which** attacks run, **where**, and **in what order** should be dynamic and based on the app. **How** each fault is injected should stay a fixed, tested set of building blocks. Here's why the line falls there.

## Why the fault mechanics stay fixed

The faults themselves come from **Android**, not from the app. Every app can be killed in the background, recreated by a configuration change, cut off from the network, have a permission revoked, or be squeezed for memory. That set is small and known.

The fix only counts if **the identical attack is replayed** after it (the PRD's core promise). If the model invented a new injection at runtime, we couldn't trust it to be repeatable or safe, and we couldn't trust a "fixed" verdict on top of it. So the injection recipes stay deterministic code. The model never writes adb commands.

## What becomes dynamic

**1. Which attack types apply, based on an app profile.** droid-monkey reads the app's manifest and the explorer's screen map, and each fault type declares when it applies:

| Fault type | Applies when the app… |
|---|---|
| Process death | has forms or deep screens (from the screen map) |
| Rotation / configuration change | has activities that are recreated by config changes (no `configChanges` override in the manifest) |
| Network loss | declares `INTERNET`, and has actions that do slow work |
| Permission revoke | declares dangerous permissions and actually prompts for them during exploration |
| Low memory / trim | holds images or lists (P1) |

**2. More building blocks, chosen per app.** These are cheap to add because each one is just a few adb settings:
- **Dark mode switch:** `cmd uimode night yes`, a configuration change like rotation.
- **Font size:** large text.
- **Language / right-to-left layout.**
- **"Don't keep activities":** Android destroys every screen you leave.
- **Low memory:** `am send-trim-memory`.
- **Airplane mode.**
- **Background idle (Doze):** for apps with background work or alarms.

A banking app with a login form, a camera app and a news reader would each get a different mix.

**3. Where and when to attack:** from the screen map, as now.

**4. Order and combinations:** chosen by the model (Block 3). It gets the app profile, the screen map and the catalogue of building blocks, and returns a ranked plan with reasons, e.g. "network loss during 'Upload' while on the 4-field form, because the upload has no visible retry". It can **combine** building blocks, such as rotating while offline, but each one stays a tested recipe.

## Proposed change

1. **`profile.py`:** read the manifest (permissions, activities and their `configChanges`, services, `targetSdk`) and combine it with the screen map.
2. **Each fault file declares `applies(profile)` and `candidates(profile)`.** `scenarios.py` then just asks every fault, so a new fault is one file and nothing else changes.
3. **Add 3 new faults:** dark-mode switch, "don't keep activities", low memory. They reuse the rotation and process-death checks.
4. **Fold in the earlier genericity fixes:** rotation timing from the map, smarter form filling, waiting for the screen instead of fixed sleeps, and silent-failure detection for network loss.

That's about 1.5–2 hours. We're roughly 3 hours ahead of schedule, so it fits without touching the Block 3 time. Should I go ahead?

Agreed. That's a better product: droid-monkey works out **what to test** and **how to attack it** for each app, and a client can add their own attacks in plain English. Here's the design, which keeps the one rule that makes fixes provable: **every attack must replay identically**.

## The design

**1. `droid-monkey analyze`: read the repo, find the flows worth testing.**
- **Without AI:** read the merged manifest (permissions, activities, `configChanges`, services, `targetSdk`), the Gradle dependencies (networking, database, camera, location libraries), and scan the source for generic risk patterns: `GlobalScope`, ViewModels without `SavedStateHandle`, network calls with no `try`, permission use without a check, and so on, each with file:line.
- **With AI (Haiku):** from the manifest, those signals and Entire's code graph, name the **user flows** that matter, such as "checkout: product → detail → checkout form → place order". Each comes with why it's risky and where it lives in the code.
- `explore` then **maps each flow to real screens** on the device.

**2. Attack types as specs built from fixed building blocks.**
- A **building block** is one fault Android can cause, implemented and verified in code: `kill_process`, `rotate`, `network_off`, `airplane_mode`, `revoke_permission`, `dark_mode`, `font_scale`, `locale_rtl`, `dont_keep_activities`, `trim_memory`, plus app steps: `tap`, `fill`, `wait`, `back`, `home`.
- An **attack type** is a short YAML spec that combines building blocks against a flow, saved in the app repo at `.droid-monkey/attacks/*.yaml` and committed:

```yaml
name: rotate_while_submitting_offline
description: Submit the checkout form with no network, and rotate while it is failing
flow: checkout
steps:
  - fill
  - fault: network_off
  - tap: place_order          # resolved against the flow's screen
  - wait: 0.5
  - fault: rotate
  - settle: 6
expect: [no_crash, keeps_fields, shows_feedback]
```

- A **validator** accepts only known building blocks with valid arguments. No shell commands and no invented actions, so every spec is safe and replays the same way every time.

**3. Two ways to create attack types:**
- **Automatically:** `droid-monkey attacks suggest`. The AI reads the analysis, the flows and the screen map, and writes specs suited to *this* app (a camera app gets permission and rotation attacks; a checkout gets network and process-death attacks).
- **From a prompt:** `droid-monkey attacks new "rotate the phone while a photo uploads on a slow network"`. The AI turns the sentence into a spec, the validator checks it, and you see it before it's saved.

**4. The four current attacks** become built-in specs, with their special handling (such as granting a permission first) kept in code.

**5. The AI loop (`run`)** plans over the built-in and custom attack types, using the analysis and flows as context.

## Order of work

| Step | Content | AI? | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `analyze` without AI: manifest, Gradle, risk patterns, app profile | No | ~45 min |
| B | Building-block library, spec format, validator, spec runner, `attacks list/show`, built-in specs. Includes the earlier genericity fixes: timing from the map, smarter form filling, waiting for the screen, silent-failure detection | No | ~1.5 h |
| C | `analyze` flows, `attacks suggest`, `attacks new "<prompt>"`, all through Haiku and traced in neatlogs | Yes | ~1.5 h, start of Block 3 |
| D | The fix loop (plan → attack → diagnose → fix → verify), unchanged from the plan | Yes | Block 3 to 4 |

That's about 3.5 extra hours. We're about 3 hours ahead of schedule, so it costs about half an hour of slack overall. If time gets tight on Monday, the cut is the extra building blocks (dark mode, font size, locale), never the AI loop.

"""Static analysis of an Android repo: manifest, dependencies and generic risk patterns. No model, no device.

The profile tells the planner what kinds of faults this app is exposed to and where in the code to look.
Every risk signal is a generic code pattern (not a known bug), reported with file:line.
"""

import json
import re
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

ANDROID = "{http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android}"

DANGEROUS_PERMISSIONS = {
    "CAMERA", "RECORD_AUDIO", "ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION", "ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION", "ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION",
    "READ_CONTACTS", "WRITE_CONTACTS", "READ_CALENDAR", "WRITE_CALENDAR", "READ_PHONE_STATE", "CALL_PHONE",
    "READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE", "WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE", "READ_MEDIA_IMAGES", "READ_MEDIA_VIDEO", "READ_MEDIA_AUDIO",
    "POST_NOTIFICATIONS", "BODY_SENSORS", "ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION", "BLUETOOTH_CONNECT", "BLUETOOTH_SCAN",
    "NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES", "SEND_SMS", "READ_SMS",
}

# Dependency keyword -> capability. Matched against Gradle files and the version catalog.
CAPABILITIES = {
    "network": ["okhttp", "retrofit", "ktor", "volley", "apollo", "grpc", "firebase-firestore", "firebase-database"],
    "database": ["room", "sqldelight", "realm", "objectbox"],
    "camera": ["camerax", "camera-camera2", "camera-core"],
    "location": ["play-services-location", "location"],
    "images": ["coil", "glide", "picasso", "fresco"],
    "background_work": ["work-runtime", "workmanager"],
    "fragments": ["fragment"],
    "compose": ["compose"],
    "viewmodel": ["viewmodel"],
    "datastore": ["datastore"],
}


@dataclass
class Signal:
    kind: str
    file: str
    line: int
    snippet: str
    why: str
    attacks: list[str]


@dataclass
class Activity:
    name: str
    exported: bool
    config_changes: list[str]
    screen_orientation: str


@dataclass
class AppProfile:
    package: str
    target_sdk: int | None
    min_sdk: int | None
    permissions: list[str]
    dangerous_permissions: list[str]
    activities: list[Activity]
    services: list[str]
    receivers: list[str]
    capabilities: list[str]
    ui_toolkit: str
    source_files: int
    signals: list[Signal] = field(default_factory=list)
    applicable_attacks: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # attack -> why it applies

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(asdict(self), indent=2))


# ---- manifest -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def find_manifest(app_dir: Path, module: str, variant: str) -> Path:
    """Prefer the merged manifest (includes library permissions), fall back to the source manifest."""
    build = app_dir / module / "build" / "intermediates"
    merged = sorted(build.glob(f"merged_manifest*/{variant}/**/AndroidManifest.xml"))
    if merged:
        return merged[0]
    return app_dir / module / "src" / "main" / "AndroidManifest.xml"


def _a(el: ET.Element, name: str, default: str = "") -> str:
    return el.get(ANDROID + name, default)


def parse_manifest(path: Path, package_hint: str) -> dict:
    root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    package = root.get("package") or package_hint
    uses_sdk = root.find("uses-sdk")
    perms = sorted({_a(p, "name") for p in root.findall("uses-permission")} - {""})
    app = root.find("application")
    activities, services, receivers = [], [], []
    if app is not None:
        for act in app.findall("activity"):
            name = _a(act, "name")
            activities.append(Activity(
                name=name if not name.startswith(".") else package + name,
                exported=_a(act, "exported") == "true",
                config_changes=[c for c in _a(act, "configChanges").split("|") if c],
                screen_orientation=_a(act, "screenOrientation"),
            ))
        services = [_a(s, "name") for s in app.findall("service")]
        receivers = [_a(r, "name") for r in app.findall("receiver")]
    return dict(
        package=package,
        target_sdk=int(_a(uses_sdk, "targetSdkVersion")) if uses_sdk is not None and _a(uses_sdk, "targetSdkVersion") else None,
        min_sdk=int(_a(uses_sdk, "minSdkVersion")) if uses_sdk is not None and _a(uses_sdk, "minSdkVersion") else None,
        permissions=perms,
        dangerous_permissions=[p for p in perms if p.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] in DANGEROUS_PERMISSIONS],
        activities=activities,
        services=services,
        receivers=receivers,
    )


# ---- dependencies -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def capabilities(app_dir: Path, module: str) -> list[str]:
    text = ""
    for f in [app_dir / module / "build.gradle.kts", app_dir / module / "build.gradle", app_dir / "gradle" / "libs.versions.toml"]:
        if f.exists():
            text += f.read_text().lower()
    return sorted(cap for cap, words in CAPABILITIES.items() if any(w in text for w in words))


# ---- source risk signals ------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SKIP_DIRS = {"build", ".gradle", "test", "androidTest", ".idea", "generated"}


def source_files(app_dir: Path, module: str) -> list[Path]:
    src = app_dir / module / "src"
    files = []
    for f in src.rglob("*"):
        if f.suffix in (".kt", ".java") and not (_SKIP_DIRS & set(f.relative_to(src).parts)):
            files.append(f)
    return sorted(files)


def _line_of(text: str, index: int) -> int:
    return text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1


def scan(path: Path, rel: str) -> list[Signal]:
    text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out: list[Signal] = []

    def add(kind: str, index: int, why: str, attacks: list[str]) -> None:
        ln = _line_of(text, index)
        out.append(Signal(kind, rel, ln, lines[ln - 1].strip()[:140], why, attacks))

    for m in re.finditer(r"\bGlobalScope\.(launch|async)", text):
        add("unscoped_coroutine", m.start(), "work is not tied to a lifecycle; it can call back into a destroyed screen",
            ["rotation", "process_death"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"class\s+(\w+)\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*:\s*\w*ViewModel\(", text):
        if "SavedStateHandle" not in text and "mutableStateOf" in text:
            add("viewmodel_state_not_saved", m.start(),
                f"{m.group(1)} keeps UI state in memory without SavedStateHandle; it is lost when the process dies",
                ["process_death"])

    if re.search(r"\b(OutlinedTextField|TextField|BasicTextField)\s*\(", text) and \
            re.search(r"\bremember\s*\{\s*mutableStateOf", text) and "rememberSaveable" not in text:
        m = re.search(r"\bremember\s*\{\s*mutableStateOf", text)
        add("input_state_not_saveable", m.start(), "input state held in remember{} is lost on recreation",
            ["rotation", "process_death"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"\bobject\s+\w+", text):
        body = text[m.end():]
        fm = re.search(r"fun\s+\w+\([^)]*\b\w+\s*:\s*(Activity|FragmentActivity|AppCompatActivity|ComponentActivity)\b", body)
        if fm:
            add("activity_passed_to_singleton", m.end() + fm.start(),
                "a singleton function takes an Activity; async work can outlive it", ["rotation"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"\.show\(\s*\w+\.(supportFragmentManager|fragmentManager)", text):
        add("fragment_transaction_from_callback", m.start(),
            "a dialog/fragment is shown through a stored FragmentManager; it throws once that Activity is destroyed",
            ["rotation"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"\b(viewModelScope|lifecycleScope)\.launch\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*\{", text):
        block = text[m.end(): m.end() + 600]
        depth, end = 1, 0
        for i, ch in enumerate(block):
            depth += ch == "{"
            depth -= ch == "}"
            if depth == 0:
                end = i
                break
        body = block[:end or len(block)]
        if not re.search(r"\btry\b|runCatching|catch\s*\(|CoroutineExceptionHandler|onFailure", body):
            add("coroutine_without_error_handling", m.start(),
                "a coroutine does work with no error handling; a thrown IOException crashes the app",
                ["network_loss"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"throw\s+(java\.io\.)?IOException", text):
        add("throws_io_exception", m.start(), "code throws IOException; callers must handle it", ["network_loss"])

    uses_guarded_api = re.search(r"\.openCamera\(|requestLocationUpdates|getCurrentLocation|MediaRecorder\(|AudioRecord\(", text)
    if uses_guarded_api and not re.search(r"checkSelfPermission|PermissionChecker|shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale", text):
        add("permission_not_checked_at_use", uses_guarded_api.start(),
            "a permission-protected API is called without checking the permission at use time", ["permission_revoke"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"put(Boolean|String)\(\s*\"?\w*(grant|permission)\w*\"?", text, flags=re.I):
        add("cached_permission_state", m.start(), "permission state is cached; it goes stale when the user revokes it",
            ["permission_revoke"])

    for m in re.finditer(r"\b(runBlocking|Thread\.sleep)\b", text):
        add("blocking_call", m.start(), "a blocking call may run on the main thread (ANR risk)", ["anr"])

    return out


# ---- the profile --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def analyze(app_dir: Path, package: str, module: str = "app", variant: str = "debug") -> AppProfile:
    manifest = parse_manifest(find_manifest(app_dir, module, variant), package)
    caps = capabilities(app_dir, module)
    files = source_files(app_dir, module)
    signals: list[Signal] = []
    for f in files:
        signals.extend(scan(f, str(f.relative_to(app_dir))))

    profile = AppProfile(
        **manifest,
        capabilities=caps,
        ui_toolkit="compose" if "compose" in caps else "views",
        source_files=len(files),
        signals=signals,
    )
    profile.applicable_attacks = applicable(profile)
    return profile


def applicable(p: AppProfile) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Which fault types apply to this app, and why. Driven by the manifest, dependencies and signals."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    hits = lambda attack: sum(1 for s in p.signals if attack in s.attacks)  # noqa: E731

    out["process_death"] = "every app can be killed in the background" + (
        f"; {hits('process_death')} state-loss signals in the code" if hits("process_death") else "")

    recreated = [a for a in p.activities if not {"orientation", "screenSize"} <= set(a.config_changes)
                 and a.screen_orientation in ("", "unspecified", "user", "sensor", "fullSensor")]
    if recreated:
        out["rotation"] = f"{len(recreated)} activities are recreated on rotation" + (
            f"; {hits('rotation')} lifecycle signals in the code" if hits("rotation") else "")

    if "android.permission.INTERNET" in p.permissions or "network" in p.capabilities:
        out["network_loss"] = "the app uses the network" + (
            f"; {hits('network_loss')} unhandled-error signals" if hits("network_loss") else "")

    if p.dangerous_permissions:
        perms = ", ".join(x.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] for x in p.dangerous_permissions)
        out["permission_revoke"] = f"declares runtime permissions: {perms}" + (
            f"; {hits('permission_revoke')} permission-handling signals" if hits("permission_revoke") else "")

    if hits("anr"):
        out["anr"] = f"{hits('anr')} blocking calls that may run on the main thread"
    return out

"""Run Claude Code headless (`claude -p`) as a tool: analysis now, the fixer in Block 3.

It runs on the user's Claude Code login. API keys are removed from its environment so it never bills the
API key droid-monkey uses for its own calls. Only stdout is parsed (global hooks may write to stderr).
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path


class ClaudeCodeError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class ClaudeResult:
    ok: bool
    text: str
    session_id: str
    cost_usd: float
    turns: int
    seconds: float
    usage: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def claude_path() -> str:
    found = shutil.which("claude") or str(Path.home() / ".local" / "bin" / "claude")
    if not Path(found).exists():
        raise ClaudeCodeError("Claude Code CLI not found: install it and log in (`claude`)")
    return found


def run(
    prompt: str,
    cwd: Path,
    allowed_tools: list[str],
    model: str | None = None,
    resume: str | None = None,
    timeout: float = 900,
) -> ClaudeResult:
    cmd = [claude_path(), "-p", prompt, "--output-format", "json", "--permission-mode", "acceptEdits",
           "--allowedTools", ",".join(allowed_tools)]
    if model:
        cmd += ["--model", model]
    if resume:
        cmd += ["--resume", resume]
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "DROID_MONKEY_API_KEY")}
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        raise ClaudeCodeError(f"claude -p timed out after {timeout:.0f}s") from e
    out = proc.stdout.strip()
    try:
        data = json.loads(out[out.find("{"):]) if "{" in out else {}
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise ClaudeCodeError(f"claude -p returned non-JSON output: {out[:300]}") from e
    if not data:
        raise ClaudeCodeError(f"claude -p failed ({proc.returncode}): {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    return ClaudeResult(
        ok=not data.get("is_error", False),
        text=str(data.get("result", "")),
        session_id=data.get("session_id", ""),
        cost_usd=float(data.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0),
        turns=int(data.get("num_turns") or 0),
        seconds=round((data.get("duration_ms") or 0) / 1000, 1),
        usage=data.get("usage") or {},
    )

"""`droid-monkey analyze`: static profile (no model) + a Claude Code read of the source -> ANALYSIS.md and flows.json.

Claude Code reads a clean copy of the source: no prose docs, scripts, git history or build output, so the
analysis comes from the code itself (docs can be stale, and a demo app's docs may describe its bugs).
"""

import json
import shutil
import tempfile
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from .profile import AppProfile
from .tools import claude_code

OUT_DIR = ".droid-monkey"
FAULT_TYPES = ["process_death", "rotation", "network_loss", "permission_revoke", "dark_mode", "font_scale",
               "locale_rtl", "dont_keep_activities", "low_memory", "airplane_mode"]

_EXCLUDE_DIRS = {".git", "build", ".gradle", ".idea", ".entire", ".claude", OUT_DIR, "monkey-report", "repro",
                 "docs", "node_modules", "captures"}
_EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES = {".md", ".txt", ".sh", ".png", ".jpg", ".webp", ".jar", ".apk", ".zip"}


@dataclass
class AnalysisResult:
    markdown_path: Path
    flows_path: Path
    flows: list[dict]
    session_id: str
    cost_usd: float
    seconds: float


def source_snapshot(app_dir: Path, dest: Path) -> int:
    """Copy only code and build config into `dest`. Returns the number of files copied."""
    count = 0
    for f in app_dir.rglob("*"):
        rel = f.relative_to(app_dir)
        if not f.is_file() or (_EXCLUDE_DIRS & set(rel.parts)) or f.suffix.lower() in _EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES:
            continue
        if f.name in ("local.properties", "monkey.yaml") or f.name.startswith("."):
            continue
        target = dest / rel
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(f, target)
        count += 1
    return count


def _profile_brief(p: AppProfile) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"package: {p.package}  targetSdk: {p.target_sdk}  minSdk: {p.min_sdk}  ui: {p.ui_toolkit}",
        f"permissions: {', '.join(x.rsplit('.', 1)[-1] for x in p.permissions) or 'none'}",
        f"runtime (dangerous) permissions: {', '.join(x.rsplit('.', 1)[-1] for x in p.dangerous_permissions) or 'none'}",
        f"activities: {', '.join(a.name.rsplit('.', 1)[-1] + (' configChanges=' + '|'.join(a.config_changes) if a.config_changes else '') for a in p.activities)}",
        f"capabilities from dependencies: {', '.join(p.capabilities) or 'none'}",
        "static risk signals (generic patterns, may include false positives):",
    ]
    lines += [f"  - {s.kind} at {s.file}:{s.line}: {s.why}" for s in p.signals] or ["  - none"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


PROMPT = """You are the analysis step of droid-monkey, a tool that attacks Android apps with real-world faults
(the OS killing the app in the background, rotation and other configuration changes, network loss, revoked
permissions, low memory) and then fixes what breaks.

The current directory is a source-only copy of an Android app. A static scan already produced this profile:

{profile}

Read the code (start from the manifest's launcher activity and follow navigation) and write two files:

1. ANALYSIS.md, for developers. Sections:
   ## What the app does: 3-5 sentences.
   ## User flows worth testing: for each flow, the user's steps, the screens involved, the data the user would lose,
      and the main code locations (file:line).
   ## Risks by flow: for each risk, the fault type, why it would break, and the code evidence (file:line). Confirm or
      reject each static signal above after reading the code; say which ones are false positives.
   ## Recommended attacks: an ordered list, most likely to find a real bug first, each one sentence.

2. flows.json, for the tool, exactly this shape:
{{"flows": [{{
   "name": "snake_case_name",
   "description": "one sentence",
   "steps": ["user-level steps, e.g. open a product", "tap Buy now"],
   "ui_hints": ["visible labels or resource ids on the flow's screens that identify them"],
   "state_at_risk": ["what the user would lose"],
   "code": ["path/File.kt:line"],
   "risks": [{{"fault": "one of {faults}", "why": "one sentence", "code": "path/File.kt:line",
              "trigger": "the user action during which the fault should hit, e.g. tap Place order"}}]
}}]}}

Rules: base every claim on code you actually read and cite file:line. Use only the fault types listed. Do not modify
any other file. Keep ANALYSIS.md under 150 lines."""


def run(app_dir: Path, profile: AppProfile, model: str | None = "claude-sonnet-5-5") -> AnalysisResult:
    out_dir = app_dir / OUT_DIR
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    profile.save(out_dir / "profile.json")

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="droid-monkey-analysis-") as tmp:
        work = Path(tmp)
        source_snapshot(app_dir, work)
        prompt = PROMPT.format(profile=_profile_brief(profile), faults=", ".join(FAULT_TYPES))
        result = claude_code.run(prompt, cwd=work, allowed_tools=["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Write"], model=model)
        md, fj = work / "ANALYSIS.md", work / "flows.json"
        if not result.ok or not md.exists() or not fj.exists():
            raise claude_code.ClaudeCodeError(f"analysis did not produce both files: {result.text[:300]}")
        flows = json.loads(fj.read_text())["flows"]
        shutil.copy2(md, out_dir / "ANALYSIS.md")
        (out_dir / "flows.json").write_text(json.dumps({"flows": flows}, indent=2))

    meta = {"session_id": result.session_id, "cost_usd": result.cost_usd, "seconds": result.seconds,
            "turns": result.turns, "model": model, "usage": result.usage}
    (out_dir / "analysis-run.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2))
    return AnalysisResult(out_dir / "ANALYSIS.md", out_dir / "flows.json", flows, result.session_id,
                          result.cost_usd, result.seconds)


def profile_dict(p: AppProfile) -> dict:
    return asdict(p)

1	# MonkeyMart analysis
2	
3	## What the app does
4	MonkeyMart is a single-activity Jetpack Compose grocery/toy shop. `MainActivity` (the only activity in the app manifest, `AndroidManifest.xml:20`) hosts a hand-rolled route switch (`MainActivity.kt:61-82`) with three screens: a product list (Shop), a product detail with a "deal" popup (Detail), and a checkout form (Checkout). The catalogue is an in-memory fake with artificial delays (`ProductRepository.kt:17-42`) and orders go to a fake backend that fails with an `IOException` when offline (`OrderRepository.kt:26-30`). Checkout can also open the camera to "scan a coupon" (`CouponScanner.kt`). The profile's `ComponentActivity` and `PreviewActivity` are not in the app manifest; they come from the `debugImplementation` compose test-manifest and tooling dependencies (`app/build.gradle.kts:54-55`) and are not user flows.
5	
6	Navigation state is `rememberSaveable` (`MainActivity.kt:62`), so the screen and product id survive rotation and process death. Everything else (detail product, form fields, order result, coupon status) is not saved in the same way.
7	
8	## User flows worth testing
9	
10	### 1. place_order (Shop -> Detail -> Checkout -> confirmation)
11	- Steps: open the app, tap a product card, wait for detail to load (5 s), tap "Buy now", fill the six fields (name, email, phone, address, city, pincode), tap "Place order", see "Order placed".
12	- Screens: ShopScreen (`shop_list`, `product_<id>`), DetailScreen (`detail_screen`, `buy_now`), CheckoutScreen (`checkout_screen`, `field_*`, `place_order`, `order_confirmed`).
13	- Data lost: the six typed form fields, the in-flight order (`placing`), and the confirmation (`orderId`) if the ViewModel is cleared. The route itself is kept.
14	- Code: `MainActivity.kt:62-81`, `ShopScreen.kt:36-37`, `DetailScreen.kt:95-98`, `CheckoutScreen.kt:34-82`, `CheckoutViewModel.kt:13-35`, `OrderRepository.kt:26-35`.
15	
16	### 2. detail_deal_popup (Shop -> Detail with deal dialog)
17	- Steps: open a product, wait on the spinner while the detail loads (5 s), see the "Deal unlocked" dialog, tap "Nice".
18	- Screens: ShopScreen, DetailScreen (`detail_loading`, `detail_screen`, `detail_name`, "Deal unlocked" dialog).
19	- Data lost: the loaded product (`remember`, not saved) so the 5 s load is repeated; the dialog may appear again or not at all.
20	- Code: `DetailScreen.kt:40-68` (DealLoader, dialog), `DetailScreen.kt:72-76`, `ProductRepository.kt:36-39`.
21	
22	### 3. scan_coupon (Checkout -> camera)
23	- Steps: on Checkout, tap "Scan coupon", grant the camera permission, see "Scanner ready: ..."; later tap "Scan coupon" again.
24	- Screens: CheckoutScreen with `ScanCouponButton` (`scan_coupon`, `coupon_status`).
25	- Data lost: the coupon status text (`remember`, `CouponScanner.kt:63`), and typed form fields if the permission change kills the process.
26	- Code: `CouponScanner.kt:33-57` (cached grant + openCamera), `CouponScanner.kt:60-86` (button), `CheckoutScreen.kt:74`.
27	
28	### 4. browse_shop (Shop list)
29	- Steps: open the app, scroll the product list, open and go back from a product.
30	- Screens: ShopScreen. Data at risk: only scroll position (list is reloaded in 800 ms). Low value.
31	- Code: `ShopScreen.kt:34-70`, `MainActivity.kt:66-68`.
32	
33	## Risks by flow
34	
35	### place_order
36	1. **network_loss / airplane_mode (crash)**: tapping "Place order" with no network makes `submit` throw `IOException` (`OrderRepository.kt:27`). `placeOrder` calls it inside `viewModelScope.launch` with no try/catch (`CheckoutViewModel.kt:31-32`) and no handler, so the exception crashes the app. The network check runs only at the start of `submit`; the later `delay(1_500)` (`OrderRepository.kt:28`) is not affected by a drop. Trigger: be offline when tapping "Place order".
37	2. **process_death (data loss)**: the six form fields and `placing`/`orderId` are plain `mutableStateOf` in the ViewModel (`CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-24`), no `SavedStateHandle`. After process death the route `checkout:<id>` is restored (`MainActivity.kt:62`) but the form is blank and "Place order" is disabled (`CheckoutScreen.kt:78`). An order in flight is silently forgotten; the user cannot tell whether it was placed.
38	3. **dont_keep_activities / low_memory (data loss)**: with "Don't keep activities" the activity is destroyed without a configuration change, so the ViewModelStore is cleared and the form is lost the same way as in risk 2, even though the process survives. Low memory behaves like process death for a backgrounded app.
39	4. **rotation (probably OK)**: the ViewModel survives rotation (`CheckoutScreen.kt:34`), the scroll state is saveable (`CheckoutScreen.kt:52`) and `orderId` is kept, so form data and the confirmation should survive. Worth one check during `placing` and on the confirmation screen, since `vm.city` is read there (`CheckoutScreen.kt:44`).
40	5. **font_scale (layout)**: the Checkout column scrolls (`CheckoutScreen.kt:52`) so it is low risk; the Detail column does not scroll (see detail_deal_popup risk 4).
41	
42	### detail_deal_popup
43	1. **rotation / dont_keep_activities (crash)**: `DealLoader.load` captures the `FragmentActivity` and starts work in `GlobalScope` (`DetailScreen.kt:57-58`), which is not cancelled when the screen leaves or the activity is destroyed. After the 5 s delay (`ProductRepository.kt:37`) it calls `activity.supportFragmentManager` and `DialogFragment.show(...)` (`DetailScreen.kt:64`). `show` uses `commit()`, which throws `IllegalStateException` if the old activity's state was already saved or the FragmentManager is destroyed. The exception propagates out of a `GlobalScope` coroutine on Main and crashes the app. Trigger: rotate (or enable don't keep activities and leave/return) within 5 s of opening a product.
44	2. **background (crash)**: pressing Home during the 5 s load runs `onSaveInstanceState` before the dialog is shown, so `commit()` at `DetailScreen.kt:64` throws the same exception (covers a `process_death`-style background/foreground cycle without the process dying). Same trigger window.
45	3. **Duplicate work and stale dialog**: each recreation starts another load (`DetailScreen.kt:74-75`) because the product is `remember`ed (`DetailScreen.kt:73`) and the old `GlobalScope` job is never cancelled. After the dialog is already open, rotation restores it and a second load can show another dialog (same tag, `DetailScreen.kt:64`). Pressing Back to Shop during the load (`MainActivity.kt:66-68`) does not cancel the job, so the dialog pops up over the Shop screen.
46	4. **font_scale / rotation (layout)**: the Detail `Column` has no `verticalScroll` (`DetailScreen.kt:86-99`) and a 96 sp emoji (`DetailScreen.kt:91`); at large font scale or in landscape the "Buy now" button can be pushed off screen with no way to scroll. Plausible, not confirmed without running.
47	5. **process_death**: restores `detail:<id>`, the 5 s spinner reappears and the load restarts (`DetailScreen.kt:73-76`); no crash, since the old coroutine died with the process.
48	
49	### scan_coupon
50	1. **permission_revoke (crash)**: after the first grant, a flag is saved to SharedPreferences (`CouponScanner.kt:36-38`, set at `:66`). Later taps check only that flag (`CouponScanner.kt:33-34`, `:76`) instead of `checkSelfPermission`. If the user revokes camera in Settings, the flag stays true, the button goes straight to `open`, and `cameras.openCamera` (`CouponScanner.kt:44`) throws `SecurityException` (lint is silenced at `:40`). Trigger: tap "Scan coupon" after revoking. Revoking in Settings also kills the process, so the form fields are lost too (risk 2 above).
51	2. **rotation (minor data loss)**: the coupon status is `remember`ed (`CouponScanner.kt:63`), so it resets on rotation. `onOpened` can also fire after the screen is gone, but it only writes state, so it is harmless.
52	
53	### browse_shop
54	1. **process_death / rotation**: the list is reloaded in 800 ms (`ShopScreen.kt:37`); only scroll position can be lost. No crash path found; the `LaunchedEffect` is cancelled correctly.
55	2. **locale_rtl / dark_mode**: dark mode is handled by the theme (`Theme.kt:38-51`); `priceLabel` formats with the default locale (`ProductRepository.kt:14`), which only changes digits. Low risk.
56	
57	### Static signals: confirmed or rejected
58	- `throws_io_exception` OrderRepository.kt:27: **confirmed**; it is the root cause of crash risk 1 (place_order).
59	- `viewmodel_state_not_saved` CheckoutViewModel.kt:13: **confirmed** (fields at `:14-19`). Rotation is safe; process death and don't-keep-activities lose data.
60	- `coroutine_without_error_handling` CheckoutViewModel.kt:31: **confirmed**; no try/catch and no `CoroutineExceptionHandler`.
61	- `permission_not_checked_at_use` CouponScanner.kt:44: **confirmed**; no `checkSelfPermission` anywhere in the file.
62	- `cached_permission_state` CouponScanner.kt:37: **confirmed**; the flag is written at `:37`, read at `:34`, and never cleared.
63	- `unscoped_coroutine` DetailScreen.kt:58: **confirmed**; `GlobalScope`.
64	- `activity_passed_to_singleton` DetailScreen.kt:57: **confirmed**; `DealLoader` is an `object` and receives the Activity from `DetailScreen.kt:75`.
65	- `fragment_transaction_from_callback` DetailScreen.kt:64: **confirmed in effect**, with a nuance: it is not a stored `FragmentManager` but `activity.supportFragmentManager` read late from a captured Activity. The failure is the same.
66	- No false positives found. The only wrong signal-adjacent entries in the profile are the `ComponentActivity` and `PreviewActivity`, which are debug-only dependency activities.
67	
68	## Recommended attacks
69	1. detail_deal_popup: rotate the device within 5 s of opening a product (rotation) to crash `DealLoader` at `DetailScreen.kt:64`.
70	2. place_order: turn on airplane mode / drop the network, then tap "Place order" (network_loss, airplane_mode) to crash on the uncaught `IOException`.
71	3. scan_coupon: grant camera and tap "Scan coupon", revoke camera in Settings, return and tap "Scan coupon" again (permission_revoke).
72	4. place_order: fill the checkout form, then kill the process in the background and return (process_death) to see the lost form.
73	5. detail_deal_popup: enable "Don't keep activities" and open a product, leave and return within 5 s (dont_keep_activities).
74	6. place_order: fill the form with "Don't keep activities" on and switch apps (dont_keep_activities) to see the form lost without a process kill.
75	7. detail_deal_popup: press Home within 5 s of opening a product to hit `commit()` after `onSaveInstanceState`.
76	8. detail_deal_popup: set a large font scale in portrait and landscape to check that "Buy now" is reachable (font_scale).
77	9. place_order: rotate while "Place order" is spinning and on the confirmation screen (rotation).
78	10. place_order: apply low memory pressure while on Checkout with a filled form (low_memory).

content.text:
`droid-monkey analyze` is built and pushed in both repos, and Claude Code writes the markdown report as you suggested.

**What it does, in two passes:**
1. **Static scan (no AI, free, instant):**
   - Reads the merged manifest: permissions, runtime permissions, activities and whether they're recreated on rotation, and services.
   - Checks which libraries the app uses.
   - Searches the code for 10 generic risk patterns, each reported with file:line.
   - Decides which fault types apply to this app.
2. **Claude Code read:** `claude -p` (Sonnet) reads a **clean copy of the source**, with no docs, scripts or git history. It confirms or rejects each signal, maps the user flows, and writes:
   - `.droid-monkey/ANALYSIS.md`: what the app does, flows worth testing, risks per flow with file:line, and recommended attacks in order.
   - `.droid-monkey/flows.json`: the same flows in a form droid-monkey can use.

**On MonkeyMart:** 4 flows, all 4 planted bugs found from code alone, and 4 extra real risks I didn't plant: pressing Home during the detail load, "Don't keep activities", a large font hiding "Buy now", and an in-flight order being lost. It took 106 seconds and used $1.01 of your Claude plan, no API credit. You can read the report in [ANALYSIS.md](.droid-monkey/ANALYSIS.md).

**Next is step B: attack types as specs.**
- **The fixed building blocks:** kill the app, rotate, network off, airplane mode, revoke a permission, dark mode, font size, right-to-left language, "don't keep activities", low memory, plus tap, fill and wait.
- **The YAML spec format,** a validator that only accepts those building blocks, and a runner that executes any spec.
- **`attacks suggest`,** which writes specs from `flows.json`. The analysis already names triggers like "rotate within 5 s of opening a product", so this is mostly translation.
- **`attacks new "<prompt>"`** for your own attack in plain English.
- **The genericity fixes** we agreed on: timing taken from the map, smarter form filling, waiting for the screen instead of fixed sleeps, and silent-failure detection.

One choice for you: should **`attacks suggest`** and **`attacks new`** also run through `claude -p`, like `analyze`? That's free on your plan but takes 30–60 seconds per call. The alternative is Haiku through the API: a few seconds and about $0.01 per call. I'd use Haiku for these short, structured calls and keep `claude -p` for jobs that need to read the repo (analysis and fixing). Which do you want?
now attacks suggest and attacksnew these should run via anthropic api

Agreed: `attacks suggest` and `attacks new` will call the Anthropic API directly (Haiku 5.5, a few seconds each, traced in neatlogs), and `claude -p` stays for the jobs that read the repo. Building step B now:

1. **Building blocks:** new verified device faults.
2. **Spec format, validator and runner:** any YAML spec can run, but only through known building blocks.
3. **`llm.py`:** the model setup (Anthropic by default, configurable in `monkey.yaml`) with neatlogs tracing.
4. **`attacks suggest` / `attacks new`:** the model writes a spec, our validator checks it, and if it's invalid the errors go back to the model for one repair attempt.

First, I'll check that the new faults work on this Android 16 emulator, particularly per-app language (for right-to-left) and airplane mode.

Yes, you can set it up and try it now. `analyze`, `explore` and `attack` all work. The attack-type specs and the agents I'm building aren't finished yet, so those commands don't exist yet.

## 1. Install the `droid-monkey` command (once)

This installs it from your local checkout, and future code changes take effect without reinstalling:

```bash
uv tool install --editable ~/Documents/neat-hack/droid-monkey
```

Then open a **new terminal tab**, so it picks up the `adb` PATH change from `~/.zshrc`, and check:

```bash
droid-monkey --help
```

## 2. Prepare the app

- The emulator is running (`adb devices` shows `emulator-5554`).
- The app's debug build is installed. From the app's folder:

```bash
./gradlew :app:installDebug
```

- Add a `monkey.yaml` at the app repo's root. MonkeyMart already has one. For another app, only this is needed:

```yaml
package: com.example.yourapp   # applicationId
module: app
variant: debug
avd: Pixel_10
# optional, for apps behind a login:
# entry_steps: ["tap text:Log in", "fill", "tap login_button"]
```

## 3. Try it (from the app's folder, e.g. `cd ~/Documents/neat-hack/MonkeyMart`)

| Step | Command | Time / cost | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free scan | `droid-monkey analyze --static-only` | instant, free | risk patterns + which attack types apply |
| Full analysis | `droid-monkey analyze` | ~2 min, ~$1 of your Claude plan | `.droid-monkey/ANALYSIS.md`, `flows.json` |
